items.title: ‘We will deactivate you’: Monu Manesar, Bajrang Dal member and murder accused, warns CJP protestors
items.summary: Monu Yadav, alias Monu Manesar, the self-styled cow vigilante and Bajrang Dal leader, appeared in an Instagram video on October 9 warning protesters against attacking police personnel at the CJP protest scheduled for October 10. In the 2:15-minute clip, Monu Manesar said he was angry over violent protesters. “Our police personnel are being beaten up, our lady police officers are being treated inappropriately,” he said. “Me and my entire team are against it.” He then threatened anyone found to have attacked police. “If we find someone from the videos we saw, if they end up in front of us, they better save themselves because we can’t be held responsible for what we will do, Jai Shree Ram,” he said. Towards the end of the clip, he added: “Our teams are ready. Our teams are active and we will deactivate you, so take care.” The video was posted on the verified Instagram profile “mohitthehindu052”, which has 1,54,000 followers. It had garnered over 1,33,000 views within 24 hours. items.title: Bengaluru police rejig: 21 new stations proposed under five new commissionerates
items.summary: Bengaluru’s police network is set for a major overhaul, with five commissionerates proposed to oversee an expanded jurisdiction and 21 new police stations planned. However, the Finance Department has approved only 11 of the proposed stations so far. According to The New Indian Express , the proposed commissionerates—Central, North, South, West and East—will be headed by officers of Inspector General of Police (IGP) or Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) rank. They will function under the Chief Commissioner of Police. Currently, Bengaluru City Police has 11 law and order divisions and four traffic divisions, each headed by a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP). Under the proposed restructuring, the five commissionerates will have a total of 14 law and order divisions and five traffic divisions. Six police stations from Bengaluru Rural district—Sarjapura, Jigani, Attibele, Anekal, Bannerghatta and Suryanagar—will be brought under the DCP (Electronics City) division of the Bengaluru South Commissionerate. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation in Bengaluru, no livestreaming of event

However unlike in the past, the convocation would neither be live streamed nor would phones be allowed inside. The convocation at NLSIU was cancelled after its students had issued a statement expressing solidarity with NALSAR Hyderabad graduates. Students at NALSAR had protested CJI Suryakant being invited for their convocation. NALSAR students had argued that they did not want to accept their certificates from the CJI as he had referred to the youth of India as ‘cockroaches’. They also criticised him for his unwillingness to listen to a plea in the Supreme Court over the police violence against protestors demanding then Union Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. However, following the dissent, Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra threatened to prohibit the enrolment of NALSAR students in the bar. items.title: NCLT suspends functioning of Mumbai Bench's court VI due to vacancies
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has ordered temporary suspension of functioning of court VI of its Mumbai Bench from October 13, citing vacancies in the posts of tribunal members. In an administrative order dated October 9, the NCLT directed that all cases pending before court VI be transferred to the five other courts of the Mumbai Bench. The suspension will remain in effect until further orders. " In view of the vacancies to the post of Members at the National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, the functioning of Court no. VI Mumbai Bench is temporarily suspended, w.e.f. 13.10.2026, until further order ," the order stated. The decision was taken with the approval of the NCLT President under Rule 16(d) of the National Company Law Tribunal Rules, 2016. According to the order, pending matters have been divided among Courts I, II, III, IV and V of the Mumbai Bench. The redistribution covers cases filed under Sections 7, 9, 10 and 95 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. items.title: Kerala HC orders fresh probe into Balabhaskar’s death, says CBI failed to examine doubts
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has ordered a fresh investigation by a senior Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officer into the 2018 death of renowned violinist Balabhaskar, criticising the agency for conducting a “casual and lackadaisical” probe into 20 suspicious circumstances flagged by the court in an earlier order. Justice G Girish, in an order dated October 9, set aside the Thiruvananthapuram Chief Judicial Magistrate Court’s December 23, 2025, decision to reject a plea for further investigation filed by Balabhaskar’s parents, K C Unni and B Santhakumari. The court directed the CBI to entrust the investigation to an officer of “proven integrity” not below the rank of Additional Superintendent of Police. It also directed the agency to issue the necessary orders within two weeks of receiving a copy of the judgment. “The course of procedure adopted by the Inspector of Police towards arriving at the aforesaid findings cannot be said to be one which behove the status of skill, tactics and expertise which are expected from a premier investigating agency like the CBI,” the court observed. items.title: Assam student’s death: Andhra and railway police probe allegations of foul play
items.summary: The death of Himashree Boro, a 20-year-old student from Assam whose body was found near a railway track in Andhra Pradesh’s Srikakulam district, remains a mystery as police continue their investigation. Himashree died soon after she reportedly informed a friend that she felt unsafe, as there were a lot of men in her coach. Her family has now alleged she could’ve been murdered, urging the police to ensure justice. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has written to Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu and Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, urging them to ensure a time-bound inquiry into her death and action against anyone found responsible. Himashree, a native of Chapaidong in Kamrup district, Assam, was a student at B Borooah College in Guwahati. She was in Andhra Pradesh as part of a dance group of eight people for a two-month assignment involving dance performances, according to her family. items.title: Dhruv Rathee, CJP leaders detained ahead of Delhi protest against CEC
items.summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) legal head Ratna Singh, and several other protesters were reportedly detained on Saturday, October 10, ahead of the party’s proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The party has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi police detained Dhruv Rathee from his residence in Sector 56, Gurugram, while Ratna Singh was reportedly detained from her residence in Delhi. Reports also said around 150 protesters had been detained by morning. Several content creators were among those detained in Dhaula Kuan, according to live updates. Mehr Pasricha, head of CJP policy division, was also reportedly detained ahead of the protest. The detentions came amid heightened security across Delhi, with police and paramilitary personnel deployed at key locations, border checkpoints, railway stations and other sensitive areas. The Ministry of Home Affairs approved the temporary suspension, ANI reported. The order covers all mobile internet services in the area. The CJP is demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has disenfranchised crores of voters along with other irregularities. A day earlier, the Supreme Court questioned the proposed closures of metro stations and train cancellations ahead of the protest, calling notifications imposing a complete ban on essential public transport “overreaching”. A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said the entire city could not be shut down in the name of managing a protest. items.summary: Communist Party of India (CPI) Rajya Sabha MP P Sandosh Kumar has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Union government to reopen Jantar Mantar for protests, stop detaining activists and ensure that citizens can exercise their constitutional right to peaceful assembly. In a letter dated October 9, Sandosh Kumar alleged that repeated attempts by protesters to reach Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in Delhi, had been met with barricades, detentions and police action. He said the protests stemmed from allegations of electoral malpractice, referred to by protesters as “vote-chori”, and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. “I am compelled to write this letter because every method of reaching out to your insensitive government has been met with barricades and lathis,” the CPI MP wrote. items.summary: Prominent YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained by Delhi Police at his Gurugram residence on Saturday morning. According to News18 , about 50 police personnel gathered outside his home late on Friday night. Delhi Police also detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) legal affairs head Ratna Singh at her residence, but according to the latest reports , she is no longer under detention. The detentions came as the CJP and the All India Students’ Association (AISA) prepared for a protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scheduled for 10 am. Police were also trying to stop people from reaching the capital in the first place. Independent journalist Raj Shekhar told Newslaundry that bus services into Delhi had been effectively halted. A Haryana Roadways employee at Ballabhgarh told him buses were being diverted at KMP towards Kundli.
